issue.title: flake-baseline gate keeps failing on historical records for nodes that have since been fixed
issue.description:
`just check-full`'s last gate, `just selection-health --fail-on-new-flake`, currently fails on athena with 13 reproducible-flake node IDs above tests/reproducible_flake_baseline.txt (window: records after the file's `# effective-after: 2026-08-15T17:22:27Z` marker).

Seven of the thirteen are the config / config-cache nodes that epic sase-ns just fixed in commit 3a22ff04f (`fix(config): isolate config cache from test-owned CONFIG_DIR`):

  tests/test_config.py::test_legacy_overlay_is_discovered_but_not_a_complete_owner
  tests/test_config.py::test_machine_overlays_require_matching_selector_and_keep_ordinary_overlays
  tests/test_config.py::test_selected_overlay_identity_cannot_be_overridden_by_other_sources
  tests/test_config_cache.py::test_clear_config_cache_forces_reload
  tests/test_config_cache.py::test_clear_config_cache_resets_config_token_time_gate
  tests/test_config_cache.py::test_current_config_token_refresh_is_single_flight
  tests/test_config_cache.py::test_explicit_invalidation_wins_race_with_background_refresh
  tests/test_config_cache.py::test_first_config_token_read_does_not_start_worker
  tests/test_config_cache.py::test_yaml_content_cache_survives_config_cache_clear

The remaining ones belong to other beads (tests/ace/tui/test_top_bar_order.py::test_override_pills_keep_narrow_top_bar_in_bounds -> sase-mp, tests/main/test_var_integration.py::test_var_cli_end_to_end..., tests/test_bead/test_cli_golden.py::test_bead_cli_golden_contract[stats], tests/test_query_profile.py::test_provider_query_schema_derives_fields_from_the_notes_fixture).

The defect: `_flake_evidence_nodeids` (tests/_test_selection_health_correlation.py) flags a node once it fails across two disjoint change sets with an *interleaved* independent pass. Interleaving is evaluated between the two recorded failures, so once that shape exists in the durable store it is permanent: a later green full lane, however many, can never clear it. Every full-run record backing these nine config nodes was written by workspaces running trees that predate 3a22ff04f (newest: ~/.sase/test-selection/gh_sase-org__sase/20260816T230240Z-e50d8a9537a1-1091606-full-run.json, recorded 2026-08-16T23:08:29Z at commit e50d8a953). The fix works -- the evidence simply cannot be retired.

Today the only lever is to hand-bump `# effective-after:` in tests/reproducible_flake_baseline.txt, which is all-or-nothing: bumping it far enough to drop the fixed config nodes also erases the still-live evidence for sase-mp and the var/bead-stats/query-profile nodes, which is exactly what the sase-mj land agent declined to do when it filed sase-mv (see that bead's SCOPE WIDENING note).

Impact: `just check-full` cannot go green on this host for any agent, on any tree, until someone resolves this by hand -- so the gate that exists to catch new flakes is currently a permanent red that every landing agent has to explain away.

Adjacent, already-solved precedent: sase-j5 taught the gate to report renamed/deleted node IDs as *stale* rather than as live flakes (`stale_flake_nodeids`, collectible-node oracle). This bead is the sibling case the same design left open: the node still collects and now passes, but its historical failure evidence is immortal.

Fix directions to weigh: record a per-node 'fixed at <commit>' retirement in the baseline file so evidence older than that commit is ignored for that node only; or treat a run of N consecutive eligible passes after the last recorded failure as retiring that node's evidence; or make `effective-after` expressible per node instead of only file-wide.

Discovered by epic sase-ns's land agent, routed from a PROPOSED FOLLOW-UP note left on phase bead sase-ns.2 (which explicitly deferred the aging-out decision to the land agent / sase-mv closer).

payload.entry: RELATED: sase-j5 — the same gate's already-fixed sibling case (renamed/deleted node IDs reported as stale via the collectible-node oracle). Its close left the 'node still collects but has been fixed' case unhandled, which is exactly this bead.

RELATED: sase-mv — the config-cache flake whose fix (commit 3a22ff04f, epic sase-ns) turned nine of the thirteen gated node IDs into historical-only evidence. Its filing note (SCOPE WIDENING, sase-mj.land) records why an effective-after bump was declined as a way to clear this class.
RELATED: sase-mp — one of the four non-config node IDs in the current 13; still-live evidence that a file-wide effective-after bump would erase along with the fixed config nodes.
